name: IDSA Criteria for Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis

citations.text: Chow AW, Benninger MS, Brook I, et al. IDSA clinical practice guideline for acute bacterial rhinosinusitis in children and adults. Clin Infect Dis. 2012;54(8):e72-e112.

validated_population: Children and adults with acute sinus symptoms (clinical practice guideline).
license_note: Published guideline criteria; not a copyrighted instrument. Question wording is original to OLA BOT.

red_flags.question: Is there swelling or redness around the eye, pain when moving the eye, or double vision or vision loss?
red_flags.help: Infection spreading to the eye area is an emergency.

red_flags.question: Do you have a severe headache with a stiff neck, or new confusion?
red_flags.help: Infection may have spread beyond the sinuses.

items.question: Have your sinus symptoms (stuffy or runny nose, facial pain or pressure) lasted 10 days or more without getting better?
items.help: Count from the first day of symptoms.

items.question: In the first few days of this illness, did you have a fever of 102.2°F (39°C) or higher?
For the first 3 to 4 days in a row, did you have thick yellow or green nasal discharge, or facial pain?
items.help: Thick, colored mucus or pain in the face every day at the start.
items.trace_label: Thick colored discharge or facial pain for first 3–4 days

items.question: Did you start to get better and then get worse again (new fever, headache, or more discharge) after about 5 to 6 days?

scoring.threshold_text: Bacterial sinusitis likely if any: (1) symptoms ≥10 days without improvement; (2) severe onset — fever ≥39°C plus thick colored discharge or facial pain for 3–4 consecutive days; (3) worsening after initial improvement. Otherwise a virus is likely.

steps.label: Severe onset (fever ≥39°C plus discharge or facial pain for 3–4 days)

bacterial.label: Bacterial sinusitis likely
bacterial.interpretation: Your symptoms meet IDSA criteria for acute bacterial sinusitis.
bacterial.recommendation: A clinician visit is advised to discuss antibiotics or a short period of watchful waiting.

care.where_detail: Telehealth or primary care visit. Urgent care if neither is available within 48 hours.
ed_redirect: Swelling or redness around the eye, or vision changes
Severe headache with stiff neck, or confusion

viral.label: Viral sinusitis likely
viral.interpretation: Your symptoms do not meet IDSA criteria for bacterial sinusitis. Most sinus infections are caused by viruses and improve without antibiotics.
viral.recommendation: Treat at home. Antibiotics are not recommended now.

care.within: Self-care; telehealth or primary care if symptoms reach 10 days or worsen
care.where_detail: Home care. Book a visit if symptoms last 10 days or you get worse after starting to improve.
ed_redirect: Swelling or redness around the eye, or vision changes
Severe headache with stiff neck, or confusion
